proposed_changes.before: East Whiteland Township municipal curative amendment under the PA Municipalities Planning Code, developed with a resident working group beginning May 2026; a Sept. 24, 2026 public hearing was set to consider adoption of the resulting ordinance
proposed_changes.after: Signed East Whiteland Township Resolution 2026-21 (March 31, 2026), invoking municipal curative-amendment protection under MPC section 609.2, 53 P.S. 10609.2, declares partial zoning invalidity concerning data-center uses and energy-generation systems and directs preparation of a cure and findings. Signed Resolution 25-2026 (April 27, 2026) makes the specific findings and renews the direction to prepare a curative amendment; it is a distinct instrument, not a second original adoption date.

facts.value: East Whiteland Township Resolution 2026-21, also referenced as Resolution 21-2026, invokes municipal curative amendment protection for data center uses and energy generation systems.
facts.supporting_quote: RESOLUTION 2026-21 … INVOKING THE PROTECTION OF THE MUNICIPAL CURATIVE AMENDMENT FOR DATA CENTER USES AND ENERGY GENERATION SYSTEMS

facts.value: The initial resolution states that it was adopted at a public meeting on March 31, 2026. The image shows completed signatures for Scott Lambert, Peter Fixler and Clinton Smith, and attestation by Manager Steven Brown.
facts.locator: Physical page 2, adoption and signature blocks
facts.supporting_quote: DULY PRESENTED AND ADOPTED … at a public meeting on the 31ST day of March, 2026.

facts.value: The Board formally declared the zoning ordinance substantively invalid in part as it relates to regulation of data center uses and energy generation systems.
facts.supporting_quote: the Zoning Ordinance is substantively invalid in part as it relates to the regulation of data center uses and energy generation systems

facts.value: The Board proposed a curative amendment and directed the Director of Planning, Zoning Officer, Township Manager, Township Solicitor and Township Engineer, with other consultants as provided, to prepare it for presentation within the time frame provided by law.
facts.supporting_quote: the curative amendment shall be presented to the Board of Supervisors within the time frame provided by law

facts.value: The initial resolution directed those officials and any other provided consultants to begin preparing a resolution for Board consideration within 30 days following the resolution's date; that resolution was to include specific findings setting forth the declared invalidity.
facts.supporting_quote: to begin preparing a resolution for consideration of the Board of Supervisors within thirty (30) days following the date of this Resolution. Such resolution shall include specific findings setting forth the declared invalidity

facts.value: The initial resolution seeks the protection of MPC Section 609.2, 53 P.S. § 10609.2. It states the Board's desire to address the specified zoning provisions without having to entertain or consider landowner curative amendments under Section 609.1, 53 P.S. § 10609.1, and without the Zoning Hearing Board having to give a report requested under Sections 909.1 or 916.1, 53 P.S. §§ 10909.1 and 10916.1.
facts.locator: Physical page 1, second and third recitals
facts.supporting_quote: without being required to entertain or consider any landowner’s curative amendment filed under Section 609.1 … and without the Zoning Hearing Board being required to give a report requested under Section 909.1 … or 916.1

facts.value: Resolution 25-2026 designates specific findings concerning the declared invalidity. It identifies the March 31 resolution as No. 21-2026 and incorporates it by reference.
facts.locator: Physical page 1, heading and first recital
facts.supporting_quote: on March 31, 2026, the East Whiteland Township Board of Supervisors approved Township Resolution No. 21-2026 … which is incorporated herein by reference

facts.value: Resolution 25-2026 states that it was adopted at a public meeting on April 27, 2026. The images show completed signatures for Scott Lambert, Peter Fixler and Clinton Smith, and attestation by Manager Steven Brown.
facts.locator: Physical pages 2–3, adoption, signature and attestation blocks
facts.supporting_quote: DULY PRESENTED AND ADOPTED … at a public meeting on the 27th day of April, 2026.

facts.value: The findings cover data centers and energy generation systems, including on-site and off-site generation for data centers and associated principal or accessory uses. The defined Data Center Uses also include on-site and off-site energy distribution and generation facilities, including generators, and associated improvements; Energy Generation Systems include generation as a principal property use.
facts.locator: Physical page 1, third recital and paragraph 1
facts.supporting_quote: on-site and off-site energy generation systems for data centers and all principal or accessory uses associated with the same

facts.value: The Board found that the ordinance did not explicitly define or regulate the uses or provide specific principal-use standards across Township districts. It found the Industrial District special-exception catchall inadequate to provide objective review criteria, and existing environmental provisions inadequate to address potential impacts including noise, vibration, glare, heat, storage and waste disposal.
facts.locator: Physical page 1, paragraphs 4–5; physical page 2, paragraphs 5–7
facts.supporting_quote: The Township Zoning Ordinance does not explicitly define or regulate Data Center Uses or Energy Generation Systems.

facts.value: The findings resolution acknowledges an obligation to provide for legitimate land uses while balancing community impacts, and renews the direction to prepare a curative amendment for presentation within the time frame provided by law.
facts.locator: Physical page 1, paragraph 3; physical page 2, paragraph 9
facts.supporting_quote: The Township acknowledges its obligation under current law to provide for all legitimate land uses … while balancing the impacts of the same on the community.

facts.value: Resolution 25-2026 states that MPC Section 609.2 provides for specific findings by resolution within 30 days following the declaration.
facts.supporting_quote: within 30 days following such a declaration, the municipality shall, by Resolution, make specific findings setting forth the declared invalidity of the Zoning Ordinance
